issue_context.title: ActiveRecord.upset generates a databases warning with MySQL 8
issue_context.body:
### Steps to reproduce

When using MySQL 8.0.34 `ActiveRecord.upset` causes a database warning 

<!-- (Guidelines for creating a bug report are [available
here](https://edgeguides.rubyonrails.org/contributing_to_ruby_on_rails.html#creating-a-bug-report)) -->

<!-- Paste your executable test case created from one of the scripts found [here](https://edgeguides.rubyonrails.org/contributing_to_ruby_on_rails.html#create-an-executable-test-case) below: -->
```ruby
ActiveRecord::Schema.define do
  create_table :products, force: true do |t|
    t.text :handle
    t.text :title
  end
end

class Product < ActiveRecord::Base
end

class BugTest < Minitest::Test
  def test_upsert
    id = Product.where(handle: handle).pick(:id)
    Product.upsert({
      id:,
      handle: handle,
      title:,
    })
  end
end
```

I think the query is generated from here
https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/f7353283fd771e99b9675bcb9394e398964195f8/activerecord/lib/active_record/connection_adapters/abstract_mysql_adapter.rb#L653-L654

### Expected behavior

The generated query should be compatible with the future database release.

### Actual behavior

Getting a warning code `1287` 

```
#<ActiveRecord::SQLWarning:
'VALUES function' is deprecated and will be removed in a future release.
Please use an alias (INSERT INTO ... VALUES (...) AS alias) and replace VALUES(col)
in the ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE clause with alias.col instead>
```

And `ActiveRecord::ConnectionAdapters::AbstractMysqlAdapter#handle_warnings` is causing visible overhead

review_comments:
Not worth doing here, more for a followup, but I wonder if it would make sense to run CI/tests with DB warnings treated as errors by default. I think it might have caught this issue way sooner.

Also we probably should backport that fix.

> Note: we have been ignoring the MySQL warning

Currently, we have a couple of places that provide a `raw_update_sql` pointing to the `VALUES(...)`, which, with this change, created a mixed query:

```
INSERT table (...) VALUES (...) as table_alias ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE x=VALUES(x)
```

The query didn't work as expected, and the expected behavior broke. We may need some way to keep using the previous behavior for a while. (I'm working on a PR unless someone beat me)

cc: @matthewd
Yes. If the `raw_update_sql` is provided, we should not try to alias, because we don't even know the alias.
Created this [PR](https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/51325) to address this issue.
